newsitem.title: UK: Got a headache? Watch those tablets, expert warns.
newsitem.headline: Got a headache? Watch those tablets, expert warns.

text.p: People who constantly take aspirin or paracetamol may be giving themselves headaches rather than keeping them at bay, a British researcher said on Thursday.

"Perhaps it is time for all analgesic packets to have a prominent health warning that daily use of headache tablets can make headaches worse'," Simon Ellis of the North Staffordshire Royal Infirmary wrote in the Postgraduate Medical Journal.
Several studies have found that persistent use of analgesics can actually bring on headache. Ellis said dependence on aspirin and paracetamol had reached "epidemic proportions".
The symptoms of chronic daily headache would significantly improve in 75 percent of cases with restrained use of painkillers and other measures such as watching diet and reducing stress, he wrote.
It can take two months for the body to purge itself of the effects of taking too many headache drugs, he added.
